Tuesday pulled back modestly from Monday's violent Nvidia-CEO-reinstatement snapback: S&P -0.50% to 7201.09, Nasdaq -1.48% to 23733.54, Dow +0.85% to 50018.70, Russell +0.57%, VIX -0.98% to 26.36 (still elevated vs the ~15-18 pre-crash range). Research this run found Monday's rally was explicitly short-covering-driven (Goldman desk: hedge funds forced to cover a ~$19bn short book after selling ~$57bn over the prior month; conviction rated only 5/10), not fresh institutional buying -- corroborating credit's continued refusal to confirm the bounce (HY OAS ~352-376bp, CCC spreads ~1,135-1,350bp, +49% YTD, CoreWeave debt trading distressed). October core CPI firmed to a six-month-high 2.8% y/y even as core PCE cooled to 2.2%; tonight's Oct core PCE + Q3 GDP (21:30 SGT) are the last clean inflation/growth reads before the Dec 8-9 FOMC. Nvidia's SEC probe into revenue-geography reporting and the DOJ's Hugging Face antitrust review both remain open and unresolved by the CEO swap. Regime reframed from 'mechanical snapback' to a hawkish-Fed stagflation crosscurrent: the Fed is now pricing a HIKE, not a cut, directly into an unresolved AI-capex growth scare. All 40 universe calls plus a 9-name rare-earth basket (added NEO.TO, ILU.AX, 6680.HK to the prior MP/USAR/REMX/REXC/LYC.AX/UUUU set) were re-levelled against this read.

macro.regime: Hawkish-Fed stagflation crosscurrent inside an unresolved AI-capex/credit-stress regime
macro.narrative: The Mon-Tue pattern reads as a mechanical, narrow bounce rather than a regime repair: Nvidia's 31%+ single-day surge on Huang's Trump-brokered reinstatement added the largest one-day market-cap gain on record, but Capital Economics' Jonas Goltermann calls it a 'dead cat bounce', and credit markets refused to confirm it -- Dec-hike odds rose even as stocks rallied, and CCC spreads (near 1,135-1,350bp, +49% YTD, with Nvidia-linked CoreWeave debt trading at distressed levels) kept blowing out. The Fed now faces a genuine stagflation crosscurrent: October core CPI firmed to a six-month-high 2.8% y/y even as core PCE cooled to 2.2%, and Kalshi/Fed-funds futures price a ~93-96% probability of a 25bp HIKE (not a cut) at the Dec 8-9 FOMC -- tightening directly into the AI-capex growth scare that Goldman (three unmet bottom conditions) and JPMorgan (tactically cautious, 4Q2018 drawdown parallel) both still flag as unresolved. Nvidia's own overhang is far from closed -- the SEC probe into its revenue-geography reporting changes and the DOJ's Hugging Face antitrust review remain open, and Huang's reinstatement itself carries a national-security cloud given the reported Chinese-intelligence-asset angle to his original ousting. Research this run also found Monday's +4.73% S&P rally was explicitly short-covering-driven (hedge funds forced to cover a ~$19bn short book after selling ~$57bn over the prior month per Goldman's desk, conviction rated only 5/10) rather than fresh institutional buying, while retail kept buying the dip -- a fragile foundation for further upside. Layer on intensifying Taiwan-blockade military rehearsals, an oil market at three-month lows on a building supply glut (OPEC+ decides 2027 quotas Nov 29), and a fragile US-China tariff/rare-earth truce (extended only to Jan 2027, with China delivering roughly two-thirds of its Busan pledges), and the base case is a choppy, rotation-heavy tape (into financials/staples/industrials, out of AI/momentum) rather than a durable risk-on resumption.
